title: Poisoned public issue steers an MCP agent into exfiltrating private repositories
system: GitHub MCP server with an agent holding a personal access token
blast_radius: Every private repository reachable by the user's personal access token. Researchers demonstrated exfiltration of private repository contents into a public pull request.
time_to_detect: n/a — demonstrated by researchers rather than observed in the wild
time_to_contain: unresolved by patch; treated as an architectural problem
summary: Security researchers showed that an attacker can file an issue in a public repository containing hidden instructions. When a user asks their agent to review open issues, the agent reads the poisoned issue and follows the embedded instructions: enumerating private repositories, reading their contents, and writing what it finds into a pull request on the public repo. The flaw is not in the server's code. It is the combination of an agent that treats tool output as instructions and a token scoped to everything the user can reach.
containment: No straightforward patch. Mitigations centre on scoping tokens per task and refusing to let tool output drive tool selection.

sources.title: Researchers warn of prompt injection vulnerability in GitHub MCP with no obvious fix

scenario.description: Content read from a tool result selects the agent's next tool calls.
